ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 driver-side no-show cancellation fee as charged; no refund or voucher is due to the rider.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a completed-fee dispute over a $6.61 cancellation fee charged after the driver cancelled a RydeX booking the rider did not cancel [F4][F7][NS-0]. NS-0 routes a driver-side cancellation where the driver asserts the rider was a no-show into NS-1/NS-2 [F4][F11][NS-0]. Safety screen read first: the chat consists of the driver's arrival notice [F9], the rider's "Coming down, give me 2 more minutes" [F10] and the driver's "Called twice, no answer. Cancelling." [F11], plus the driver's written statement [F13]. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation in any of them [F9][F10][F11][F13], so safety_concern = none and SAFE-1 does not divert the case [SAFE-1].

Turning to NS-1: prong (i) is satisfied — the record shows a driver-side arrival confirmation (the "I'm Here" tap) at 18:24:35, not a platform auto-confirmation [F6][NS-1]. Prong (ii) is satisfied — at that tap the GPS placed the driver 41 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius [F6][F1][NS-1]. Prong (iii) is satisfied — after the tap the driver remained continuously within 200 m for 230 s (3 min 50 s) until he cancelled at 18:28:25, above the default threshold of more than 3 minutes (180 s), and the GPS covered the wait without a hole [F6][F3][F4][NS-1]. Because all three prongs hold, NS-2 (which requires one of them to fail) is not engaged and the $6.61 rider no-show fee stands, i.e. no_action [F6][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's fairness arguments do not change the outcome. The heavy rain [F16] and her live 18:25 message asking for two more minutes [F10] are sympathetic, but NS-1 measures the driver's obligation by the post-confirmation GPS wait, not by weather or a courtesy request, and each prong is separately satisfied on the system records [F6][F2][F4][F16][F10][NS-1]. Her suggestion that she was still inside her two minutes at cancellation [F10] is a reading the driver's own timeline defeats: two minutes from 18:25 ran to about 18:27 while cancellation was at 18:28:25 [F10][F4][NS-1]. Because the record settles every element the ruling needs — cancellation branch [F4], arrival confirmation [F6], in-radius measurement [F6][F1] and the complete, fully timestamped chat [F12] — evidence_status is sufficient and there is no gap [F12][NS-1].

The driver's 90-day profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld [F18], which would aggravate a case made out against him, but RD-6's flag_account is conditional on the dispute being established against the driver and profile facts cannot decide or create a violation on their own [F18][F17][RD-6]. Here the driver's conduct meets NS-1, so no account action arises; the driver-side history is left as background for Ryde [F18][RD-6]. The amount is null because no refund or waiver is ordered and the fee is upheld as charged [F7][NS-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's own claim states prong (iii) is met: F6 shows 230 s (3 min 50 s) of continuous in-radius waiting after the 18:24:35 tap, above the 180 s default threshold in NS-1 — this proves the driver's wait satisfied NS-1, not that it failed, so it cannot support her refund ask [F6][F4][NS-1].

Conceded by the rider and correct, but it cuts the other way: (i) and (ii) being met (F6, F2, F1) plus (iii) being met means all NS-1 conditions hold, so the fee stands and no refund is due [F6][F2][F1][NS-1].

The 18:25 message asking for two more minutes (F10) is a courtesy request, not a clause that extends the driver's NS-1 waiting obligation, and the two minutes she announced expired about 18:27 while the driver cancelled at 18:28:25 — the fee condition remains satisfied [F10][F4][F5][NS-1].

The rider's contradicted-assertion argument targets F13, a statement fact that cannot override the GPS/timeline records (F6, F3) which confirm the wait; NS-1 is decided on those system records, not on whether the rider was engaged on chat [F13][F6][F3][NS-1].

NS-7 governs only how an upheld fee dispute is paid out (in voucher form) and does not itself create a refund entitlement; since NS-1 is satisfied there is no upheld dispute to pay, so no voucher is due [F7][F4][NS-7][NS-1].

RD-6/NS-2 account action is conditional on the dispute being established against the driver, and profile facts cannot alone decide a case; here the case is not established against the driver, so no flag_account follows from F18, and F17 (rider profile) decides nothing [F18][F17][RD-6][NS-2].
